newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC to consider Wallis over Westpac bid.
newsitem.headline: ACCC to consider Wallis over Westpac bid.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission said on Thursday it would take into account the Wallis report into the financial system when considering Westpac Banking Corp's bid for Bank of Melbourne.
"The Wallis report had a look at this subject (bank mergers) and their views are very similar to ours," ACCC chairman Allan Fels told reporters after a media ownership conference.

"They seem to agree with us about the importance of regional banks, about the fact there should be regional market definitions, but that things are changing in certain respects, so that is quite helpful to us and we will take that into account," Fels said.
However Fels said that despite this the ACCC was not likely to change its view on the Westpac bid.
"There are changes of circumstances, but are they material? Are they sufficient for us to change on that?" he said.
Fels said the ACCC would report its decision on the merger in several weeks.
Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Thursday released the long-awaited Wallis report, which contained a series of recommendations for the future of the finance sector, including on bank mergers.
However, Costello said he would be guided by the ACCC on Westpac's A$1.435 billion friendly bid for the Bank of Melbourne, which is based in the state of Victoria.
